audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart rows 3-6 disagreed with content and packet (Ekko 4-5, Veigar at 6, first item, 2+ items); breakdown.cooldowns had no digit; bleed bullets; the W-shield, R-untargetable-heal and E auto-reset tell were understated in the full layer.
audit.why: Kit: Ekko R 110/80/50s untargetable rewind heal (heal + untargetable flags), W 22-14s shield+stun anomaly, E 9-7s dash with auto-reset flag, Q 9-7s projectile.
audit.corrected: Chart aligned with rewritten whys, real cooldowns added, R-heal deny in dosFull[1].d, auto-reset tell in dontsFull[0].d, W anomaly in enemyWin.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Ekko wins by chunking with Timewinder, stun-diving off W's anomaly, and undoing every losing trade with his R.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-stack on cooldown and double-stack off cannon waves. The curve is the matchup.
edits.after: He still picks trades with Q poke and Phase Dive stickiness pre-ult — Q-stack on cooldown, double-stack cannons.

edits.before: Primordial Burst online — anyone under half is now a math problem with one answer. Count R damage out loud.
edits.after: His E dash lands him inside your cage — hold E for the dive and stun-W-R kills him before Chronobreak matters.

edits.before: Luden's spike: cage-W-Q-R deletes squishies who touch the wall. Your zone is a courtroom now.
edits.after: Stacked Q makes the cage-combo a one-shot — his all-in eats a stun that kills through the rewind.

edits.before: Late Veigar IS the scaling argument: cage the choke, burst the carry, and let infinite AP write the closing statement.
edits.after: Any engage onto you dies to E-W-R on contact — infinite AP out-bursts the rewind heal and he must play around you.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Event Horizon (self-cage) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — 110s at rank 1 (50s at rank 3); it erases your kill and bursts back, so save the final damage for after it. - Your E Event Horizon (20s at rank 1) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

edits.before: Cage his step-up, W the edge-stun, Q-auto, and walk — a half-bar trade that also deposited three stacks into the curve.
edits.after: His R heals off damage taken in the last few seconds — R him the instant he dips under half, before the rewind banks it.

edits.before: That is Ekko’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: His E roll into the auto wind-up is the tell — step back now.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: At half HP his W-empowered autos shred you and E closes the gap in a blink — stacks aren't worth trading into his kill timers.
